overviewParagraphs: Chi Linh Golf is uniformly regarded as the hardest course in Northern Vietnam — a title it wears with pride. Carved through a dramatic pine-forested valley in Hai Duong Province, the layout's significant elevation changes, narrow corridors, and true bentgrass greens combine to create an unrelenting challenge.

Earning the nickname "the Dalat of the North" for its cool mountain air and rugged terrain, the course winds through ravines and along ridgelines with little room for error off the tee. The fast, true bentgrass surfaces — rare in Northern Vietnam — demand precision on every approach.

For the serious discerning golfer who wants to put their game to the ultimate test, Chi Linh Golf is the benchmark. AGS regularly programmes it on challenge-focused itineraries for groups seeking a genuine step up from the standard Hanoi resort circuits.

curatorBriefHtml: Chi Linh Golf (often known as Chi Linh Star) sits in a pine-clad valley in Hai Duong Province, halfway along the highway linking Hanoi and Ha Long Bay. Across 36 holes (27 original championship holes plus a newer 9), the course has long been regarded as one of Northern Vietnam’s sternest ball-striking exams — famous for undulating valley fairways, elevated greens, and penal water hazards that demand conservative target golf off the tee.

Because Chi Linh sits roughly 75 minutes east of central Hanoi and 75 minutes west of Ha Long Bay, it works brilliantly as a transit round on a multi-stop Northern Vietnam tour. Instead of losing a travel day sitting in a vehicle between Hanoi and your Ha Long Bay cruise or hotel, AGS schedules a morning round at Chi Linh with luggage stored safely in your private touring vehicle, delivering you straight to Ha Long Bay by late afternoon.

Playability peaks from October to April when cool northern air keeps the bentgrass-influenced putting surfaces crisp and fast. Players who struggle with forced carries should move up one tee box — from the Blue Tees (7,160 yards), Chi Linh plays every inch of its card.

scorecard.verdict: Northern Vietnam's pioneering championship facility. Set in a wooded valley surrounding a large natural lake, Chi Linh features dramatic elevation changes and tough tiered greens that reward accurate approach play.

faqs.q: Why do Northern Vietnam itineraries include Chi Linh Golf between Hanoi and Ha Long Bay?
faqs.a: Chi Linh sits directly on the Hanoi–Ha Long corridor (about 75 minutes from either hub), making it the most efficient way to convert a transfer day into a full championship round without doubling back.

faqs.q: How difficult is Chi Linh Golf for mid-handicap touring golfers?
faqs.a: Chi Linh is one of Northern Vietnam’s more demanding layouts due to tight hillside fairways, elevated green complexes, and frequent lake carries. Mid-handicappers enjoy the course far more from the White Tees rather than stretching back to the 7,160-yard Blue Tees.

faqs.q: When are course conditions best at Chi Linh Golf?
faqs.a: Autumn through early spring (October–April) offers cool, dry playing weather and the smoothest green speeds. Summer rounds (June–August) are lush and playable with an early morning tee time.

faqs.q: Can AGS handle luggage transfers during a Hanoi-to-Ha Long round at Chi Linh?
faqs.a: Yes. Your dedicated private touring vehicle and driver remain on-site at the Chi Linh clubhouse with your suitcases and golf bags securely stowed, then continue directly to your Ha Long Bay hotel or cruise pier after your round.
